solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cold, strangely barren American city (8)

indicatorNotes.strangely: BARREN is set out in a strange order

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A chilly, desolate city somewhere in the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue points you at the USA, but the city is the capital of Australia; 'American' only supplies the final A.
annotation.definitionFit: Canberra is the purpose-built capital of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

entries.clue: Network supporting 100 people in a group (4)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue, LAN sits beneath C and holds it up

annotation.surface: Some computer network links up a hundred members of a group.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer the piece that 'supports' another goes underneath it, so the network comes after the 100.
annotation.definitionFit: A clan is a Scottish-style kinship group, many families claiming one shared ancestor.

entries.clue: One chap standing up to welcome old woman (5)

indicatorNotes.standing up: in a down clue, standing up means the letters read bottom to top

annotation.surface: A man gets to his feet to greet an elderly woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Woman' in crosswords often clues a girl's name, and here it is the biblical Naomi.
annotation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female given name, borne by Ruth's mother-in-law in the Old Testament.

entries.clue: Estimated bonus accompanying top deal, possibly (12)

indicatorNotes.possibly: TOP DEAL could possibly be rearranged into something else

annotation.surface: Guessing at how big a bonus will come with a top business deal.
annotation.walkthrough: The business surface makes 'top deal' look like a single phrase, but it is seven letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to estimate by extending known data.

entries.clue: Peppery veg is excellent — kinda! (6)

annotation.surface: A half-hearted verdict on a hot-tasting vegetable: it's sort of great.
annotation.walkthrough: Both pieces are slang, which matches the casual 'kinda'; ISH is now used as a word on its own for 'sort of'.
annotation.definitionFit: The radish is a vegetable with a sharp, peppery taste.

entries.clue: Partly aloof or moody appearance (4)

indicatorNotes.Partly: the answer is only part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the third

annotation.surface: A person who looks somewhat distant or sulky.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer spans three words: aloo(F OR M)oody.
annotation.definitionFit: Form means outward shape or appearance.

entries.clue: Insurance policy excluding first item is too old (7)

indicatorNotes.excluding first item: the first letter is left out

blocks.note: COVERAGE without its first letter C

annotation.surface: An insurer refuses a policy because the applicant is too old.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'too old' sound like an insurer's refusal, which fits the answer's meaning neatly.
annotation.definitionFit: Overage means over the age limit, too old.

entries.clue: Minute details excitedly given out in the wrong way (8)

annotation.definition: given out in the wrong way
annotation.surface: Someone eagerly pores over the fine points of a matter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minute' reads as tiny (my-NOOT) with 'details', but it is the time unit, abbreviated M; a misdealt hand of cards has been given out wrongly.
annotation.definitionFit: To misdeal is to deal cards out wrongly.

entries.clue: Somewhere that’s out of this world to an escapist, somehow (5,7)

annotation.definition: Somewhere that’s out of this world

indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters are made into the answer somehow

annotation.surface: A dreamer's idea of paradise, a place far from ordinary life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out of this world' usually means wonderful, but here it is literal: a space station orbits beyond Earth. The fodder includes 'to', which looks like a link word.
annotation.definitionFit: A space station is a place out in space, literally beyond this world.

entries.clue: A book published on the topic of … (5)

blocks.note: a book that is out has been published

annotation.surface: The start of a description: a book has been published on the subject of something.
annotation.walkthrough: The trailing dots invite you to finish the sentence, but the definition is the words just before them.
annotation.definitionFit: About works as a preposition introducing a subject, as in a film about war.

entries.clue: Extremely divisive newspaper reviews cause unhappiness (7)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: the press is newspapers and the coverage they give

annotation.surface: Harsh, polarised reviews in the papers upset people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cause unhappiness' looks like a result of the reviews, but it is a verb phrase standing for DEPRESS.
annotation.definitionFit: Depress is a transitive verb: bad news depresses you, making you feel low and gloomy.

entries.clue: Senior officer’s colleague is cut off (12)

annotation.surface: A top police officer's partner has been isolated.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S is used as a letter S, and 'is' is only a link; DI is Detective Inspector, a senior police rank in Britain.
annotation.definitionFit: Disassociate is a verb for severing a link, as when a party distances itself from a disgraced member.

entries.clue: Our cat’s unusually taking hours to fall asleep (5,3)

indicatorNotes.unusually: the letters appear in an unusual order

blocks.note: H = hours, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A pet cat is strangely slow to drop off to sleep.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder takes H on board before it is rearranged. Crash out is informal for falling asleep quickly.
annotation.definitionFit: Crash out is informal slang for dropping off suddenly and heavily, typically when exhausted.

entries.clue: Right editor with very good tabloid (3-3)

annotation.surface: A right-wing editor running a popular paper.
annotation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid newspaper, named for the red mastheads of papers like The Sun and the Mirror.
annotation.definitionFit: Red-top is British slang for a tabloid newspaper.

entries.clue: Dismally empty, filthy house (7)

indicatorNotes.empty: empty out the middle, leaving just the outer letters

annotation.surface: A bleak, bare and dirty home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests a building, but it means a ruling family, as in the House of Windsor.
annotation.definitionFit: A royal house is a dynasty, a line of rulers from one family.

entries.clue: A person who dresses smartly also (2,4)

blocks.note: an old slang word for a fashionably dressed person, 5 letters

annotation.surface: A sharp dresser is included too.
annotation.walkthrough: A swell is dated slang for a sharp dresser; the split moves one letter, so A SWELL becomes AS WELL.
annotation.definitionFit: As well is an adverbial phrase meaning in addition or too, like its synonym.

entries.clue: Stick plug in this spot (6)

blocks.note: to plug a product is to advertise it; a plug is an ad

annotation.surface: An instruction to push a plug into a particular socket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests an electric plug, but it is a promotional mention, an advert.
annotation.definitionFit: Adhere is the formal verb for glue or tape clinging to a surface.

entries.clue: Pantomime element of opera with element of ballet? (4,3,5)

annotation.surface: A question about what goes into a pantomime: bits of opera and bits of ballet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface treats pantomime as a stage show, but here it means a fuss or needless palaver, which is what a song and dance is.
annotation.definitionFit: Both a pantomime and a song and dance mean an overblown fuss.

entries.clue: Take it easy, initially coming home sick (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the first letter of each of the next two words

blocks.note: first letters of Coming and Home

annotation.surface: Advice to someone who has come home feeling unwell: rest.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'Take it easy' sound like advice to the patient, which is also the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To chill is informal for relaxing or taking it easy.

entries.clue: Anglers regularly departing for a long time (4)

indicatorNotes.regularly departing: letters depart at regular intervals, leaving every other one

annotation.surface: Fishermen often head off for long stretches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For a long time' reads like part of the surface, but only 'a long time' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ages is a colloquial plural for an extended period, as in waiting ages for a bus.

entries.clue: Disgusting stink about histrionic display (7)

indicatorNotes.about: turn BO about, back to front

blocks.note: to make a scene is to put on a dramatic display

annotation.surface: A revolting smell surrounding someone's melodramatic outburst.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning' in the surface; here it turns BO round.
annotation.definitionFit: Obscene fits in its broader sense of morally repugnant or revolting, not just indecent.

entries.clue: Decorating job is somewhat cosmetic, in general (5)

indicatorNotes.is somewhat: the answer is some of the letters that follow

blocks.note: the letters start near the end of the first word and run into the third

annotation.surface: A remark that home decorating tends to be only skin-deep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decorating' suggests painting a room, but the job is decorating a cake: cosmet(IC, IN G)eneral.
annotation.definitionFit: Icing is the job of decorating a cake with sugar coating.

entries.clue: Small dogs ultimately aren’t so annoyingly boisterous (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the final letter of each following word

blocks.note: last letters of arenT sO annoyinglY boisterouS

annotation.surface: In the end, little dogs are not so irritatingly lively.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in aren't is ignored, so its last letter is T. Toy dogs are breeds kept small as pets.
annotation.definitionFit: Toys are very small breeds of dog, such as toy poodles.

entries.clue: Artist using only reds, weirdly (8)

annotation.surface: A painter who strangely works in nothing but red.
annotation.walkthrough: Sir Joshua Reynolds was an 18th-century English portrait painter.
annotation.definitionFit: Joshua Reynolds was a famous English artist.
